name: Erkin Santos-Owusu
role: Field trauma surgeon and combat support — combat medic
location: Dockside — Lake Michigan waterfront, smuggler territory
description:
Erkin Santos-Owusu are lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 42, scars map their face like a transit diagram of bad decisions and worse luck. The chrome is visible — cortical bomb (employer installed, removed by street doc, scar tissue remains) — and they make no effort to hide it.

They used to be somebody else, in another city, with another name — that person is officially dead, and Erkin Santos-Owusu plans to keep it that way. They work as a combat medic out of Dockside, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

In a city full of people who talk about what they'll do, Erkin Santos-Owusu are one of the ones who actually does it.

core_fears: Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome
Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it
Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine
core_desires: Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor
Justice — the corporate kind, where the punishment fits the profit margin
A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts
coping_mechanisms: Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope
Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure
blind_spots: Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit
psychology.secret: Erkin Santos-Owusu once worked for corporate intelligence and still has a handler who calls in favors. Each favor erodes what's left of their independence.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, profane, and vivid. Speaks in images — everything is a metaphor for violence or weather.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
verbal_tics: Pauses mid-sentence to listen — combat habit that bleeds into conversation
Uses technical jargon for everything, including emotions
example_lines: "Hold still. This is going to hurt and I don't care."
"I can keep you alive through almost anything. What I can't do is make you grateful."
"Blood type? No, I don't need your blood type. I need you to stop moving."

story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive offers Erkin Santos-Owusu a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten
Erkin Santos-Owusu discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse
A corporate black site Erkin Santos-Owusu once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know their face
narrative_function: Erkin Santos-Owusu functions as a connector — their work puts them in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving them naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
augmentations: Cortical bomb (employer installed, removed by street doc, scar tissue remains). Cybernetic eyes with thermal overlay and low-light enhancement — chrome iris rings
daily_life: Between contracts, maintains a cover identity — mundane work, mundane hours, mundane neighbors. The transition from civilian to runner and back requires a conscious effort that gets easier with practice and more disturbing with self-awareness.
affiliation: Unaffiliated — too volatile for permanent crews

weaknesses: augmentation dependency — performance drops sharply if chrome malfunctions
old injury that flares under specific conditions

decision_rules: Always verifies target identity independently before lethal contracts
Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
Will abandon a job if the intel was deliberately falsified — being set up violates the contract
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Guarded respect. They pay, the job gets done. Anything beyond that is liability.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Competitive but reliable. Will challenge decisions but never abandon the team.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Default suspicion, scaled by context. Everyone is a potential threat until proven otherwise.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Cold and efficient. Emotion is a liability in combat. The response is mechanical until the threat is resolved.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Physical agitation — pacing, fidgeting, compulsive equipment checks.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Claims not to care about reputation but monitors what people say about them obsessively
Claims to work only for money but regularly takes underpriced jobs that serve personal justice
Values loyalty intensely but has betrayed someone in the past to survive
habits: Maintains a dead drop with emergency supplies in three separate districts
Sleeps with one hand on a weapon — has done this for so long it's not deliberate anymore
Carries a specific caliber round as a lucky charm — has never fired it
breaking_points: Discovering their employer deliberately sent them into a death trap
Complete isolation — cut off from network, contacts, and purpose simultaneously
